message.content: The exact number of mitochondria varies widely among cell types and depends on the cell’s metabolic demands. In most mammalian cells you’ll find somewhere between **50 and 500 mitochondria**. Cells with high energy requirements—such as skeletal muscle fibers, cardiac myocytes, or neurons—can contain several thousand mitochondria per cell. Conversely, cells with lower energy needs may have fewer than 50.
